_meta.central_question: Does any existing Aurora mechanism allow prior experience/consequence to alter the inputs, context, weighting, interpretation, or selection process that determines a later (constraint, dimension) coordinate?
_meta.method: Hand-curated from direct source reads and live code execution this session, cross-checked by an independent background research pass covering 6 subsystem areas. Every edge below is traced data flow (a variable produced by one function consumed by another), not co-import or shared terminology.
_meta.selector_definition: The coordinate selector is SemanticMatcher.match(expression: str) -> MatchResult (aurora_reflexive_interpreter.py:662-696), which fixes (constraint, dimension, nc_name) from UtteranceParser.parse(expression) plus three static lookup tables (FRAME_TO_CONSTRAINT, STANCE_TO_DIMENSION, ROLE_TO_DIMENSION) plus _find_nc()'s scoring against the static manifold directory.

selector_inputs.name: UtteranceParser.parse(text)

All lookup sets (_TRUE_FILLER, _STRUCTURAL, _WORD_ROLES, _PHRASE_ROLES, _TOPIC_OVERRIDES, etc.) are class-level literals assigned once at class-definition time, never reassigned anywhere in the repo (confirmed by exhaustive grep for reassignment/monkeypatch).

selector_inputs.evidence: Module-level dict literal, never mutated anywhere in the repo.

selector_inputs.name: _find_nc() candidate scoring

candidate_feedback_paths_searched.evidence: aurora_reflective_readdressing.py's own docstring: 'No permanent belief, rule, or code change is made here' -- it reads UtteranceParser as a consumer, never writes to its tables. internalize_correction/apply_correction/_absorb_user_correction/needs_correction/run_backprojection_step individually checked: none reference the six selector-input identifiers.

scripts/bridge_ledger_to_noncomps.py DOES write real consequence data (from aurora_state/pressure_experiences.jsonl, populated by the live PressureExperienceLedger) into each matching noncomp JSON file's development_tracking.history array. This is a genuine consequence-to-manifold-file write. However: (a) it is a manually-invoked, __main__-gated offline script, never called from any automatic boot/runtime path; (b) development_tracking is never read by _find_nc, ManifoldFieldMap, NoncompManifold.stream_slots, or entries_for_axis -- it has zero consumers anywhere in the codebase. A real write into a field nothing reads.

All three are genuine, real, consequence-fed persistent stores -- but every one of them is written or read AFTER match() has already fixed (constraint, dimension) for that call (aurora_reflexive_interpreter.py:911 runs before lines 930-970). None is ever consulted by UtteranceParser.parse() or _find_nc() for a FUTURE call's selection. This is the exact conservation-report finding re-confirmed, extended here to 6 additional subsystems with the same negative result.

relation_to_object_promotion_finding.evidence: ConstraintLink's own docstring: 'A promoted pair (or pair-of-pairs) that has proven reliably effective. Once promoted, it becomes a re-usable trace element.' Its parents field can hold ability ids OR link ids, and depth>1 exactly when a parent is itself a Link -- i.e. genealogy already has a real, existing, non-hypothetical mechanism where a promoted relation becomes an object that can itself be an endpoint of a later, higher-order relation.
relation_to_object_promotion_finding.caveat: This is a genuine existing example of the general 'relation promoted to reusable object' pattern the directive's Part VI asks about -- but it lives entirely in genealogy's atom-pair space, is structurally and causally disconnected from sub_law_c / the manifold coordinate under primary investigation (per the prior system-wide conservation report's confirmed finding that ReflexiveInterpreter has zero data flow into genealogy), and does not by itself support any claim about the manifold's proposed depth-three space. Reported as a precedent pattern, not as evidence for depth-three.
